text: Upstash Agent Skills 面向 DSH 和其他编码助手，提供产品技能指南与 MCP 集成。它将 Redis、QStash、Workflow、Vector、Search、Box、Blob、Ratelimit 等指南装入技能目录，并在 DSH 注册技能提供器、账户 MCP 客户端和 /upstash-login 凭据命令。代理可据此编写应用集成，或通过认证的 MCP 工具管理账户资源。技能无需凭据；DSH 账户操作需邮箱和 API Key。

Upstash Agent Skills gives coding agents SDK guides for Redis, QStash, Workflow, Vector, Search, Box, Blob, and Ratelimit. Its DSH bundle registers those skills and an authenticated account MCP client, configured with /upstash-login. The guides work without credentials.
我想给 Node.js 项目加一个 Redis 缓存，最好有适合无服务器环境的接入指南。
怎么安排一个无服务器后台任务定时运行，并在失败时重试？
我需要一个能跨函数超时继续执行、支持等待和重试的工作流方案。
有没有云端隔离环境可以让 AI agent 跑命令、改代码和预览网页？
我想在 API 路由里按用户或 IP 限流，并控制请求频率。
怎样把文档做成向量检索或语义搜索，供 RAG 应用查询？
I need a serverless queue that can deliver HTTP jobs later and retry failed requests.
How can I give an AI coding agent a remote cloud workspace with a shell and browser?
I want to add full-text or semantic search to my application without managing a search cluster.
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「Redis 应用指南」：提供 JavaScript/TypeScript Redis 指南，涵盖缓存、会话、键值存储、队列和事务。
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「消息与持久工作流指南」：分别提供 QStash 消息调度和 Workflow 持久执行的 SDK 说明，涵盖延迟投递、重试、步骤、回调与长时间等待。
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「云端 Box 指南」：介绍用 TypeScript/JavaScript 或 Python 创建沙盒容器，并使用 agent、shell、文件系统、Git、定时任务和浏览器。
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「搜索与向量指南」：介绍全文、语义和混合搜索，以及向量写入、相似度查询、命名空间和元数据过滤，可用于为应用加入检索或 RAG。
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「Blob 文件存储指南」：说明 S3 兼容对象存储、浏览器直传、签名读取和分段上传，帮助代理为应用编写文件上传与私有读取集成。
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「账户 MCP 接入」：DSH 在邮箱和 API Key 均配置后通过 stdio 启动 Upstash MCP Server，并在凭据更新时重新挂载；代理可调用账户管理工具。
Upstash Agent Skills 的功能「保存 MCP 凭据」：在 DSH 会话中调用 /upstash-login，输入邮箱和 API Key；命令将两项写入凭据管理器，随后触发 MCP 客户端连接。
Upstash Agent Skills 使用前须知：DSH 的账户 MCP 客户端只有在邮箱和 API Key 都已保存后才会启动；技能指南本身可不配置凭据使用。凭据命令为 /upstash-login。
Upstash Agent Skills 使用前须知：DSH 通过 npx 获取 @upstash/mcp-server，首次启动新版本需要网络；账户 MCP 服务地址为 mcp.upstash.com。

upstash-skills README · Upstash Agent Skills：Connect your AI coding agent to Upstash. This repo ships **skills** (per-SDK instruction packs your agent loads on demand) and the **plugin manifests** that install them — and now the **Upstash MCP server** — into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Zed, and any Agent Skills–compatible client.

upstash-skills README · The Upstash agent surface：- **Skills** — packaged instructions and CLI references for each Upstash SDK (Redis, QStash, Workflow, Vector, Search, Box, Blob, Ratelimit). No credentials needed. → [docs](https://upstash.com/docs/agent-resources/skills)
- **MCP server** — live tools to query, debug, and manage your account. Two ways to run it:
  - **Remote (hosted)** — `https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp`, streamable HTTP, authenticated with OAuth (browser consent, on first use) or a developer API key header. Nothing to install.
  - **Local (stdio)** — [`@upstash/mcp-server`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@upstash/mcp-server) run with `npx`, authenticated with your account email + a developer API key.

upstash-skills README · The Upstash agent surface：→ [docs](https://upstash.com/docs/agent-resources/mcp)
- New here? Start with the [AI Tools overview](https://upstash.com/docs/agent-resources/overview), and see [Install by agent](https://upstash.com/docs/agent-resources/clients) for full per-client setup.

upstash-skills README · What's in this repo：- **`skills/upstash-*/`** — the per-SDK skill sources (each has a `SKILL.md`). Edit these.
- **`skills/upstash/`** — the combined skill, **generated** from all the sources by `npm run build`. Never hand-edit it (see [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)).
- **Plugin manifests** — `.claude-plugin/`, `.codex-plugin/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, `gemini-extension.json`, and the portable [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) `plugin.json` + `mcp.json`. They make the repo installable as a plugin/extension. **These plugins now bundle the remote Upstash MCP server (OAuth), so installing the plugin sets up the skills *and* the MCP in one step** — no separate MCP configuration for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Gemini CLI.
- **`zed-extension/`** — a Zed MCP server extension (Rust → Wasm).
- **`assets/`** — branding used on the plugin card, read by Codex (`interface.logo` / `interface.composerIcon`) and Cursor (`logo`). Claude Code, Gemini CLI and the Agent Plugins schema have no icon field.

upstash-skills README · Install：Installing through a **plugin** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI) sets up both the skills and the remote MCP server — approve the MCP's OAuth consent on first use. The skills-only installers (Agent Skills CLI, OpenCode, Zed) install skills; add the [MCP server](#mcp-server) separately if you want live account access, or use [`npx upstash`](#one-command-claude-code-codex-cursor-gemini-cli-vs-code-copilot-cli-opencode), which sets up both.
upstash-skills README · Install：For the full, up-to-date per-client instructions, see [Install by agent](https://upstash.com/docs/agent-resources/clients).

upstash-skills README · One command (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode)：```bash
npx upstash
```

Run in a terminal, the [Upstash CLI](https://github.com/upstash/cli) detects your agents and installs the plugin where the agent supports one (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI), otherwise the remote MCP server plus the `upstash` skill (VS Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode). Either way the agent gets both the skills and the MCP server, which signs in with OAuth on first use. The per-agent steps below do the same by hand.

upstash-skills README · One command (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode)：From an agent or a script, name the agent and skip the prompts:

```bash
npx -y upstash setup --yes --claude        # or --codex, --cursor, --gemini, --vscode, --copilot, --opencode
npx -y upstash setup --yes --mode mcp      # MCP server + skill everywhere, no plugins
```

upstash-skills README · Cursor (skills + MCP)：We are waiting for this plugin to be accepted to the official
[Cursor Marketplace](https://cursor.com/marketplace). Once listed, it can be installed
from **Customize** in the Cursor sidebar, and it brings both the skills and the MCP server.
Until then, `npx upstash setup --cursor` installs the same plugin locally (reload the Cursor window afterwards).

upstash-skills README · Gemini CLI (skills + MCP)：Gemini CLI loads this repo as an [extension](https://geminicli.com/docs/extensions/) — the manifest is `gemini-extension.json` at the repo root; every skill under `skills/` and the remote MCP server are picked up automatically:

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/upstash/skills
```

upstash-skills README · OpenCode：OpenCode loads [Agent Skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills) from `.agents/skills/` in a project
and `~/.config/opencode/skills/` globally, which is where the Agent Skills CLI writes them for
OpenCode:

```bash
upstash-skills README · Available in every project：npx skills add upstash/skills --agent opencode --global

upstash-skills README · Or just this project：npx skills add upstash/skills --agent opencode
```

OpenCode exposes the installed skills to the agent through its native `skill` tool, so the
agent loads only the sub-skill relevant to the task at hand. For live access to your account
(create databases, inspect QStash logs, and so on), add the [MCP server](#mcp-server) as well, or run
`npx upstash setup --opencode`, which installs the skill and adds the MCP server in one step.

upstash-skills README · Zed：Zed loads [Agent Skills](https://zed.dev/docs/ai/skills) from `.agents/skills/` in a project
and `~/.agents/skills/` globally, which is exactly where the Agent Skills CLI writes them:

```bash
upstash-skills README · Available in every project：npx skills add upstash/skills --agent zed --global

upstash-skills README · Or just this project：npx skills add upstash/skills --agent zed
```

The skills then show up in Zed's Agent Panel, and the agent can load them on its own or via
`/upstash`. Zed's extension marketplace carries languages, themes, debuggers, snippets, and MCP
servers, but has no channel for skills, so the CLI is the only way to install them. The Zed
extension in `zed-extension/` covers the [MCP server](#mcp-server) instead.

upstash-skills README · Agent Skills CLI：```bash
npx skills add upstash/skills
```

upstash-skills README · DeepSeek Harness：Installs the skills **and** the [Upstash MCP server](#mcp-server) in one step. Requires
`pnpm` on your `PATH`.

```bash
upstash-skills README · Install into a profile (`web` is the one `dsh web` boots)：dsh plugin --profile web add github:upstash/skills
section: Install into a profile (`web` is the one `dsh web` boots)

upstash-skills README · Start the harness：dsh web
```

Then store your Upstash credentials from inside a session:

```
/upstash-login YOUR_EMAIL YOUR_API_KEY
```

Credentials are stored in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` and the MCP server connects as
soon as both are set. The skills work without them.

upstash-skills README · MCP Server：Installing a plugin above already wires up the remote MCP server. Set it up on its own when you
use a skills-only installer (OpenCode, Zed) or a client without a plugin.

**Remote (recommended)** — no install; OAuth on first use, or pass a developer API key header
(`email:API_KEY`) for headless/CI. Create a key at
[Console → Account → API Keys](https://console.upstash.com/account/api).

upstash-skills README · Updating an existing skill：1. Edit the files in the individual skill folder (e.g. `skills/upstash-qstash-js/`).
2. Run `npm run build` to regenerate `skills/upstash/`.
3. Commit both the source changes and the regenerated output.

upstash-skills README · Adding a new skill：1. Create a new folder under `skills/` (e.g. `skills/upstash-redis-js/`).
2. Add a `SKILL.md` with the standard frontmatter (`name` and `description`) and any supporting files.
3. Run `npm run build` — the new skill will be picked up automatically.
4. Commit everything.

upstash-skills README · Changing the combined skill header：The frontmatter and introductory text for `skills/upstash/SKILL.md` comes from `scripts/header.md`. Edit that file, then run `npm run build`.

upstash-skills README · Updating the plugin version：When making a release, bump the `version` field in every manifest that carries one: `plugin.json` (the portable [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) manifest), `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, and `gemini-extension.json`.

upstash-skills README · The Zed extension：`zed-extension/` is a Zed MCP server extension that runs [`@upstash/mcp-server`](#mcp-server).
It is a Rust crate compiled to WebAssembly, and it is only about the MCP server — Zed extensions
cannot carry skills.

```bash
cd zed-extension
rustup target add wasm32-wasip2   # once
cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip2
```

upstash-skills README · The Zed extension：Test a local build with `zed: install dev extension` and point Zed at `zed-extension/`.
Open Zed on a folder while testing — context servers are project-scoped, so with no project
open (or one whose worktree fails to open) the server never starts and the panel sits on
"Connecting Server..." until Zed's 60s timeout.

upstash-skills README · The Zed extension：To publish or update it, open a PR against
[`zed-industries/extensions`](https://github.com/zed-industries/extensions) that adds this repo
as a submodule under `extensions/mcp-server-upstash` and an entry in `extensions.toml`:

```toml
[mcp-server-upstash]
submodule = "extensions/mcp-server-upstash"
path = "zed-extension"
version = "0.1.0"

upstash-skills README · The Zed extension：The `version` there has to match `version` in `zed-extension/extension.toml`, so bump both
together. `zed-extension/LICENSE` is a symlink to the repo's MIT license — Zed requires a
license at the extension path, not just at the repo root, and rejects the PR in CI without one.

upstash-skills README · The Zed extension：> Zed [plans to deprecate MCP server extensions](https://zed.dev/docs/extensions/mcp-extensions)
> in favor of the official MCP registry. If that lands, publishing `@upstash/mcp-server` to
> [registry.modelcontextprotocol.io](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/) replaces this
> extension.

upstash-skills README · Scripts：| Script | Command | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `build` | `npm run build` | Regenerates `skills/upstash/` from all individual skills. |
| `check` | `npm run check` | Runs the build, then fails if there is a git diff — used in CI to ensure the generated output is committed. |
upstash-skills README · CI：The GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/check.yml`) runs `npm run check` on every push and PR. If you forget to run `npm run build` before pushing, CI will fail.
